title: Pasta e Lenticchie
subtitle: Italian lentil and pasta soup
excerpt: Pasta e lenticchie is a thick Italian soup of green or brown lentils and small pasta. The lentils are cooked with a soffritto of onion, carrot, celery, and tomato, then the pasta is added directly to the pot. A drizzle of raw olive oil at the end is not optional.
sourceNotes: Pasta e lenticchie is a staple of southern and central Italian cooking, particularly associated with Campania, Lazio, and Puglia. Lentils are eaten throughout Italy on New Year's Eve and New Year's Day as a symbol of good fortune. The dish is among the oldest combinations in Italian cooking and appears in numerous regional cookbooks from the 19th century onward.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the pasta. The lentil base freezes well for up to 3 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the lentil base ahead. Add pasta when reheating, as it absorbs the broth and becomes soft if left.

content.text: Pasta e lenticchie is a thick soup of lentils and pasta: deeply flavoured from a well-made soffritto base, thickened naturally as the lentils soften into the broth. Green or brown lentils do not need soaking and cook in about 30 minutes. The pasta goes in for the last 10 minutes and absorbs the lentil broth as it cooks. A generous drizzle of raw olive oil before serving makes a significant difference.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, celery, garlic, and rosemary. Cook for 12 to 15 minutes until soft and lightly golden.

Add the tinned tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes. Add the lentils and stock. Season with salt, bring to a simmer, and cook for 30 to 35 minutes until the lentils are completely tender and starting to soften into the broth.
Remove the rosemary sprig. Add the pasta and cook for the time on the packet, stirring frequently. The soup should be very thick.
Taste, adjust salt, and serve with a generous drizzle of raw olive oil in each bowl.

Lentils are eaten throughout Italy, but pasta e lenticchie is most at home in Campania, Lazio, and Puglia. In Italy, lentils are eaten on New Year's Eve and New Year's Day as a symbol of prosperity: the small discs resemble coins. The Umbrian black lentils from the town of Castelluccio are considered the best in Italy and are much prized for this soup.
